messages:
maya: Quick bring-up from this morning: ran rbig-13B across us-east / us-west / eu-west on A100 and H100, fp16 vs int8. Sharing p50/p95 + throughput and routing notes.

maya: Results table (summary):
```
CONFIG          | REGION   | GPU   | PREC  | P50(ms) | P95(ms) | QPS (tokens/s)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
rbig-13B-fp16    | us-east  | A100  | fp16  | 28      | 110     | 14.2k
rbig-13B-int8    | us-east  | A100  | int8  | 22      | 92      | 18.5k
rbig-13B-fp16    | us-west  | A100  | fp16  | 30      | 120     | 13.7k
rbig-13B-int8    | us-west  | A100  | int8  | 24      | 100     | 17.2k
rbig-13B-fp16    | eu-west  | A100  | fp16  | 45      | 260     | 9.8k
rbig-13B-int8    | eu-west  | A100  | int8  | 36      | 210     | 12.4k
rbig-13B-fp16    | us-east  | H100  | fp16  | 20      | 78      | 19.6k
rbig-13B-int8    | us-east  | H100  | int8  | 16      | 65      | 25.1k
rbig-13B-fp16    | eu-west  | H100  | fp16  | 32      | 180     | 15.3k
rbig-13B-int8    | eu-west  | H100  | int8  | 25      | 140     | 20.8k
```

maya: High-level takeaways: eu-west p95 is much worse than US regions even with same batching/warmup. p50 deltas are small.
ajay: Nice table. So tail looks dominated by network/routing?
sophia: Did you check edge path? any extra proxies in eu?
maya: I dug in: packet traces + traceroutes show eu-west often goes via edge-router-2 -> proxy-gw -> model-node under load. That adds ~70-120ms at tail. us-east uses a direct fabric route.
kevin: That matches the large p95 gap. Were kernels/ops also different?
maya: I ran a quick kernel sweep on A100 int8 in eu-west (two candidates): CUTLASS baseline vs our fused-attn.
maya: CUTLASS: p50 36ms, p95 210ms. fused-attn: p50 40ms, p95 195ms. Fused reduced p95 a bit but increased p50 slightly. Throughput similar. So ops help but can't remove the big network tail.
ajay: Makes sense. If routing adds a 100ms noisy hop it's going to dominate p95.
sophia: Proposal: 1) canary 5% traffic pinned to fabric-direct (no proxy) 2) sticky routing for warm paths to see effect on tail.
maya: Agreed. Also will add per-request hopcount and kernel/quant tags to logs so we can correlate hopcount vs latency.
infra-bot: canary-deploy: started canary -> fabric-direct (5%), config id cdr-2077. Monitoring: perf, infra-health, fallback enabled.
kevin: FYI cost note: H100 int8 has much better tail in eu. Consider reserving a small H100 pool for tail-sensitive routes in eu-west. Might be cheaper than overprovisioning A100.
sophia: +1 on routing policy: tail-sensitive -> prefer H100 or fabric-direct. Add as a rule in routing-config.
ajay: Can you capture 4h/12h/24h snapshots for p50/p95 and hopcount distribution? will want plots.
maya: Yep — I'll push snapshots to the perf dashboard and post short summaries at 4h/12h/24h. Will include: p50/p95, qps, hopcount histogram, kernel variant usage.
maya: Quick note: fused-attn looks promising for reducing variance; keep it enabled in canary as a variant to test combined effect with fabric-direct.
kevin: If the canary halves p95 in eu, we can roll and add H100 as fallback. Otherwise we need infra fixes.
sophia: Also add a small synthetic tail test (10k requests at 90% concurrency) to reproduce under controlled load.
maya: Will run synthetic tail test and include results in 4h snapshot.
ajay: Thanks maya — very actionable.
sophia: Thanks!
kevin: nice work. :rocket:
